papers.title: Flexible megahertz low-power complementary circuits based on nanoscale organic transistors
papers.summary: The stringent low-power requirements of wearable electronics systems can be met only by combining p-channel and n-channel transistors in a complementary circuit topology. For circuits based on organic thin-film transistors (TFTs), this calls for improvements in n-channel TFT performance. We report on flexible low-voltage nanoscale n-channel organic TFTs fabricated using a recently developed high-performance small-molecule semiconductor. The TFTs have on/off current ratios greater than 10 8 and subthreshold swings below 200 millivolts per decade. Nanoscale n-channel and p-channel organic TFTs were integrated into inverters that display small-signal gains up to 175, noise margins up to 80%, static power consumption as low as 10 −12 watts, and characteristic signal-delay time constants as short as 60 nanoseconds (at 3 volts). These are the best-performing flexible organic TFT–based complementary inverters reported to date.

papers.title: CMOS surprises
papers.summary: Nature Electronics, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41928-026-01748-4 Unexpected effects are still being discovered in complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) circuits, and the results could have implications for the advance of quantum computing.

papers.title: Roseburia intestinalis counteracts TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis
papers.summary: Interactions between serum metabolites and vascular endothelial cells directly influence atherosclerotic lesions. It is essential to identify and understand the effects of the complex profile of serum metabolites on vascular pathology. In this study, we found that coronary lesion severity positively correlated with serum levels of the organophosphate ester tris (2-butoxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), while TBEP levels inversely correlated with gut Roseburia intestinalis abundance. Western diet supplemented with TBEP substantially exacerbated atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E −/− ( ApoE −/− ) mice. We found that TBEP enhanced AMP-activated protein kinase α (AMPKα) phosphorylation, reduced nuclear translocation of active sterol regulatory element–binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) fragments, suppressed Patatin-like phospholipase domain–containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) protein expression in endothelial cells, and increased lipid deposition. Oral R. intestinalis supplementation reduced fecal and serum TBEP levels and attenuated TBEP-driven atherosclerotic lesions. We highlight that TBEP aggravates endothelial lipid accumulation and atherosclerosis, suggesting that targeting gut microbiota may serve as a promising strategy against TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.
